PELLHAM — Pellham Borough Council approved the harbour levy by 19 votes to 6 on Thursday evening, according to people familiar with the matter.

The vote came at the council's regular session on 14 March 2024. Councillor Odette Varnham, chair of the Pellham Harbour Committee, moved the motion.

The levy sets a charge of 2.4% on commercial mooring and cargo-handling fees. It is projected to raise £1.8 million over five years.

The result is recorded as a roll-call vote in the certified minutes of the 14 March meeting, which those people said confirm the 19-to-6 tally.

The measure passed with a clear majority of the chamber. Further details on implementation were not immediately available.

Meridian Brief will update this item as information emerges.
